signal_summary.notes: Google Trends 'Trending Now' surfaced one breakout (Porsha Williams) — rejected as celebrity/off-category. No trend candidate cleared thresholds purely on search_velocity this run; the 3 retained candidates clear on source_credibility + opportunity_score (thin SERP coverage), consistent with a slower health news cycle. candidates.topic: Washington Post investigation: many FDA-ordered post-market drug and device studies never completed
candidates.recommended_angle: Explainer: 'Why does the FDA let some drugs and devices stay on the market without finishing the safety studies it required?' — translate the WaPo investigation into a consumer-facing accountability piece with a checklist of how to look up a drug's post-market study status.
candidates.why_now: WaPo's 9/17 investigation surfaces a structural FDA oversight gap with direct patient-safety relevance; no competitor has run a consumer-facing explainer version yet — clear SERP gap.
candidates.primary_headline: The FDA Required These Safety Studies. Years Later, Many Still Aren't Done.
candidates.next_steps: Corroborate via a second outlet or FDA's own openFDA post-market requirement database before publishing; identify 1–2 named drugs/devices from the WaPo piece to anchor the explainer.
integrity_flags: Single-source (WaPo) story — confidence capped low until corroborated.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Single tier-1 source (WaPo); moderate search velocity; structural policy finding with narrow prior coverage.
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: Thin consumer-facing SERP coverage of post-market study accountability angle; high editorial gap vs. existing pieces.
candidates.discover_score_reason: Tier-1 source, policy relevance, patient-safety angle; moderate trend velocity does not justify higher discover.
candidates.notes: High opportunity given thin consumer-facing SERP coverage of this specific angle.

candidates.topic: Federal research funding cuts leave aging Alzheimer's study participants without results
candidates.recommended_angle: Patient-impact framing (not partisan): what happens to a long-running Alzheimer's study — and its aging participants — when the funding that analyzes results disappears mid-study. Ground in research-continuity/patient-access terms, not political critique.
candidates.why_now: Guardian's 9/17 report ties an active funding disruption to real patients awaiting individual study results — a concrete, ongoing harm distinct from generic policy debate.
candidates.primary_headline: These Seniors Volunteered for an Alzheimer's Study. They May Never Learn the Results.
candidates.next_steps: Seek a second, non-Guardian source or the study's own institutional statement to raise confidence before publishing; confirm study name/sponsor.
integrity_flags: Single tier-2 source (Guardian); frame carefully to stay inside allowed categories (aging/longevity + patient access) and out of excluded 'pure political healthcare opinion.'
candidates.trend_score_reason: Tier-2 source (Guardian), policy/funding disruption angle; moderate search velocity; aging/longevity topical fit.
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: Patient-impact framing offers clear SERP gap vs. generic policy coverage; human-interest angle under-served in health news.
candidates.discover_score_reason: Guardian tier-2 source, aging audience relevance, patient-access angle; lower than P2/WaPo due to source tier.
candidates.notes: Single source confidence rating; verify study details before publishing.

fact_check.checked_against: Guardian headline 'Hundreds of ageing Americans may not get results of Alzheimer's study due to Trump cuts' (09/17/2026) in Google News Radar

candidates.topic: UT Southwestern identifies metabolite that fuels aggressive brain tumor growth
candidates.primary_entity: UT Southwestern brain tumor metabolite discovery
candidates.recommended_angle: Explain what the metabolite does in plain-language terms and what it could mean for future glioblastoma treatment — clearly framed as early-stage discovery science, not a near-term treatment.
candidates.why_now: UT Southwestern's 9/16 press release on preclinical metabolite discovery offers SEO opportunity for 'brain tumor metabolite' queries with minimal competitor coverage.
candidates.primary_headline: Scientists Discover a Key Metabolite Fueling Aggressive Brain Tumor Growth
candidates.next_steps: Confirm named journal/DOI before publishing; contact institutional press office or study lead; clarify this is preclinical/discovery-stage, not a treatment breakthrough; seek neuro-oncologist or cancer metabolism researcher for expert framing.
integrity_flags: Single-institution press release; confirm named journal/DOI before publishing and clarify this is preclinical/discovery-stage, not a treatment breakthrough.
candidates.trend_score_reason: Single institutional press release; discovery-stage science with limited search velocity; solid long-tail SEO opportunity.
candidates.opportunity_score_reason: Explainer format fills SERP gap for 'brain tumor metabolite' queries; institutional credibility supports scheduled placement.
candidates.discover_score_reason: Institutional press release, neuro-oncology audience fit, discovery-stage framing; moderate discover due to single source and preclinical stage.
candidates.notes: Estimated 600-800 words; neuro-oncologist or cancer metabolism researcher expert recommended; discovery-stage finding, not a treatment — do not overstate clinical relevance.
